images.title: Using the protractor correctly
images.purpose: Show the correct way to place a protractor: centre on the vertex and one arm along the 0 line.
images.composition: One large protractor semicircle centred with an angle drawn inside it.
images.exact_structure: One protractor drawn as a plain semicircle with its straight edge at the bottom. A reddish purple #CC79A7 dot at the middle of the straight edge is the vertex and the protractor centre. One horizontal arm in teal #0072B2 runs from the vertex along the straight edge through the 0 line at the right. A second teal #0072B2 arm rises from the vertex at 35°, with a small amber #E69F00 arc between the arms. Exactly 1 protractor, 2 arms, 1 arc.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
an arm that does not start at the centre dot
images.takeaway: Centre on the vertex, one arm on 0, then read.
images.description: A protractor with its centre dot on the angle vertex, one arm along the 0 line and the other arm reading 35°.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the centre dot and the 0 line before reading the angle.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture of the angle itself; one clean image carries it.
